problem_description: soc: espressif: ppa: fix the leftover block check for rotation and ARGB. Scale, rotate and mirror bypasses the macro block order when the last block would be smaller than the 2D-DMA FIFO, which the engine never counts, so the transfer would not end. The check sized the blocks from the unrotated input and took ARGB8888 output as 16 bits per pixel cut 64 pixels wide, so it missed a 40x200 RGB565 block turned a quarter, or a 100x100 block written as ARGB8888. problem_description: Bluetooth: Controller: nordic: Fix preempted ECB use with EasyVDMA. A do_ecb() call preempted by an ISR that runs do_ecb() itself, such as the radio ISR resolving a TargetA while a thread encrypts with bt_encrypt_le(), relies on the preempting call clearing ECBDATAPTR to start over. On SoCs with EasyVDMA (nRF54L, nRF54H20, nRF7120), the key is in separate registers and ECBDATAPTR is IN.PTR, which is set after the key: - Preempted between its key writes, the call keeps the words that the preempting call wrote in place of its own earlier ones, then sets IN.PTR, and returns a result computed with a mix of both keys. - Preempted after setting IN.PTR but before starting, it starts the ECB with IN.PTR cleared, which the nrf54l15bsim model reports as a hard fault on hardware. Count the attempts, so that a call starts over whenever another one ran in between, and have each call restore the pointers it found instead of clearing them, so that a preempted call always starts with its own. Tested with a scratch build that runs a nested ecb_encrypt() at each point of do_ecb(), as a preempting ISR would: on nrf54l15bsim, preemption during the key writes gave a wrong result and preemption between the IN.PTR write and the start hit the model's NULL IN.PTR error, and now every point gives the right result; on nrf52_bsim every point gives the right result before and after. The bsim ll/conn, ll/bis, ll/edtt, ll/multiple_id and ll/advx tests pass on both, and host/security and host/privacy on nrf52_bsim. Not run on hardware.

problem_description: Bluetooth: Controller: Fix builds with BT_CTLR_CRYPTO disabled. BT_CTLR_CRYPTO selects whether the Controller provides bt_rand(), bt_encrypt_le() and HCI LE Encrypt, and with them the ECB driver that the Zephyr Link Layer also needs for LE encryption and privacy. Its LLLs indicate support for both features whenever the Controller has crypto support at all, so a build with BT_CTLR_CRYPTO=n still enables them: - LE encryption derives the session key with ecb_encrypt(), which the Nordic LLL builds only with BT_CTLR_CRYPTO since commit a66baa1101ad ("Bluetooth: Controller: Introduce BT_CTLR_CRYPTO_SUPPORT"), so every such build with BT_CTLR_LE_ENC fails to link. On rv32m1_vega, the board enables the CAU3 driver that it uses only with BT_CTLR_CRYPTO. - Privacy calls bt_rand() and bt_encrypt_le() through rpa.c, which are then the Host's: from the radio ISR, and from HCI command handling, where with BT_HOST_CRYPTO_PRNG=n bt_rand() sends HCI LE Rand from within the command being handled and deadlocks. HCI-only builds have no bt_rand() at all and stop at configuration time, as BT_CTLR_PRIVACY selects BT_RPA, which depends on BT_HOST_CRYPTO or BT_CTLR_CRYPTO. Have the Nordic and OpenISA LLLs indicate support for LE encryption and privacy only with BT_CTLR_CRYPTO, and say so in its help text. Tested with BT_CTLR_CRYPTO=n: samples/bluetooth/peripheral builds on nrf52840dk/nrf52840, nrf51dk/nrf51822, nrf54l15dk/nrf54l15/cpuapp and nrf52_bsim, samples/bluetooth/central on nrf52840dk/nrf52840, hci_ipc on nrf5340dk/nrf5340/cpunet, hci_uart on nrf52840dk/nrf52840, and tests/bluetooth/init with prj_ctlr_central_priv.conf on rv32m1_vega/openisa_rv32m1/ri5cy. The default configurations of these builds are unchanged.

problem_description: net: mii: fix MMD ACR post-increment function values. The function field of the MMD Access Control Register (register 13) is two bits wide, at bits 15:14. MII_MMD_ACR_DATA_RW_POS_INC and MII_MMD_ACR_DATA_W_POS_INC shifted 0x10 and 0x11 into that field, where binary 10 and 11 were meant. Truncated to 16 bits they came out as 0x0000 (the address function) and 0x4000 (data, no post increment). Use 0x02 and 0x03 instead, giving 0x8000 and 0xC000. These match the behavior named in the comments above the macros and the values Linux uses (MII_MMD_CTRL_INCR_RDWT and MII_MMD_CTRL_INCR_ON_WT). Nothing in the tree uses these two macros, so no behavior changes. Tested by compiling the header on the host with static assertions for all four function values: the two for the changed macros fail before this change and pass after it. Not built in a west workspace, not run through twister and not run on hardware.

problem_description: Bluetooth: Classic: AVRCP: Fix TG vendor response queue corruption. bt_avrcp_tg_vendor_tx_work() hands a single-packet response to bt_avctp_send() while the buffer is still the head of tg->vd_rsp_tx_pending, and removes it from that list only afterwards. By then bt_avctp_send() has linked the same buf->node into the AVCTP TX list, so with another response pending the removal leaves the list with a tail but no head: the responses queued behind it and every vendor dependent response the TG sends later are never sent, and their buffers are lost. Remove the buffer from the pending list before handing it to AVCTP. Tested with a Bumble CT against the BR shell on native_sim over the simulated BR/EDR controllers: with two CHANGED notifications queued behind a fragmented GetElementAttributes response, only the first one arrived and no later response did; with the fix all of them arrive.

problem_description: soc: espressif: pm: fix kernel uptime loss on light sleep wakeup. The light sleep exit hook unmasked interrupts before the kernel accounted the slept ticks. A wake ISR that armed a timeout could then preempt the idle-exit announce with a stale alarm and drop the rest of the sleep from the kernel clock. Fix it by keeping interrupts masked in the exit hook and no longer selecting PM_STATE_SET_IRQ_UNLOCKED, so the idle thread unmasks them after the slept ticks are announced. problem_description: drivers: dp: swdp_bitbang: fix nRESET polarity for GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW. The driver's runtime sw_set_pins() / sw_get_pins() handlers treat the CMSIS-DAP DAP_SWJ_Pins nRESET bit as a Zephyr logical pin value, but the CMSIS-DAP specification defines that bit as the raw electrical level driven onto the line (bit=0 -> drive low / asserted, bit=1 -> drive high / deasserted). The mismatch only shows up when a board overlay declares reset-gpios with GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW (the natural choice for active-low nRESET): the polarity flag is applied a second time inside gpio_pin_set_dt(), so the runtime assert/deassert end up inverted. With GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH the runtime behaviour is correct but the GPIO_OUTPUT_INACTIVE setting in sw_port_on() leaves the line driven low on init, holding the target permanently in reset between SWD transactions. Translate the raw level into the polarity-aware logical level in both sw_set_pins() and sw_get_pins(), so boards can use the conventional GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW for the reset-gpios property and the line ends up electrically released when idle, asserted only while DAP_SWJ_Pins asks for it, and deasserted again afterwards. Bench-validated on NUCLEO-H723ZG (probe) -> NUCLEO-WL55JC (target): without this fix, an explicit pyocd target.reset(NSRST) leaves NRST pinned electrically low (DHCSR.S_RESET_ST stays set across reads post-reset). With this fix and reset-gpios = <... GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>, connect_mode=under_reset, target.reset(NSRST) and DAP_SWJ_Pins all operate as the CMSIS-DAP spec describes.

problem_description: boards: nxp: mimxrt1180_evk: fix CM7 flash-boot load offset. Commit bfa8f8aad02f ("boards: nxp: fix multicore image load addresses") stopped adding the FlexSPI mapping base on top of DT_REG_ADDR() for the CM7 code partition, since zephyr,mapped-partition now resolves that address through devicetree ranges translation on its own. It updated the RAM-boot LMA adjustment and the CM7 boot address in soc.c, but missed the sibling FLASH_LOAD_OFFSET default used for CONFIG_CM7_BOOT_FROM_FLASH, which kept using the already-absolute partition address as if it were still a flash-relative offset. As a result, the CM7 image built for CONFIG_CM7_BOOT_FROM_FLASH=y linked at FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS (0x28000000) plus that doubly-counted offset (0x28720000), landing at 0x50720000, well outside the FlexSPI window. west flash then fails to program the remote domain. Compute FLASH_LOAD_OFFSET the same way BUILD_OUTPUT_ADJUST_LMA already does for the RAM-boot case: subtract the (also mapped) base of zephyr,flash from the code partition's address instead of using it directly. Built and flashed samples/drivers/mbox (sysbuild, CONFIG_CM7_BOOT_FROM_FLASH=y) on mimxrt1180_evk/mimxrt1189 hardware: west flash now completes without error and the CM7 core boots from external flash, exchanging mbox messages with CM33 on the console.

problem_description: twister: fix the job server being ignored by Ninja 1.13. Ninja 1.13 became a GNU make job server client, but on POSIX it accepts the job server only as a named pipe. problem_description: Bluetooth: Classic: fix discovery stop while resolving names. BT_DEV_INQUIRY stays set while remote names are being resolved, but the controller has already reported Inquiry Complete by then, and the Host is only told to issue Inquiry Cancel before that event (Core Specification 6.3, Vol 4, Part E, Section 7.1.2). If the controller fails the cancel then, bt_br_discovery_stop() returns that error with the flag still set and the name resolution still running, and bt_br_discovery_start() keeps returning -EALREADY until the last name request completes. Only send Inquiry Cancel when no remote name request is outstanding. A name is requested from report_discovery_results(), which runs on the Inquiry Complete event, so a result in RESOLVE_REMOTE_NAME_RESOLVING is itself the record that the inquiry has finished. The inquiry can also complete while the cancel is in flight. When that completion starts no name request it clears the flag, and a failure with the flag already clear is the stop that has just happened, not an error to report. When it starts one the flag stays set until the last name request completes, so the failure is returned and the caller can stop again, which then skips the cancel and tears down.

problem_description: boards: shields: arduino_giga_display_shield: fix illegal PLL3 config. PLL3 was configured with div-m = 16 and mul-n = 110, giving a 1 MHz reference and a 110 MHz VCO. This is outside both legal operating modes of the STM32H747 PLL (VCOL: 150-420 MHz VCO, VCOH: ref >= 2 MHz). Since commit 00f0eb822bf7 ("drivers: clock_control: stm32h7: fix incorrect VCO configuration logic") the configuration is rejected with -ERANGE, and stm32_clock_control_init() returns before applying the bus prescalers and switching SYSCLK to PLL1. The M7 core is left running from HSI (64 MHz instead of 480 MHz) and peripherals such as the console UART compute their dividers from DT rates that no longer match the actual clock tree, resulting in wrong baud rates. Use div-m = 8 and mul-n = 110 (2 MHz reference, 220 MHz VCO, VCOL) and double the P/Q/R dividers so the outputs are unchanged, keeping the 27.5 MHz LTDC pixel clock on pll3_r.

problem_description: net: http: server: Size the pollfd table for H3 listen sockets. A service that supports HTTP/1 or HTTP/2 together with HTTP/3 opens two listen sockets, a TCP one and a QUIC one, but the pollfd table reserved only one slot per service. The extra listen sockets pushed the client slots, and with few H3 stream slots the last client slot, past the end of fds[]. Reserve two slots per service when HTTP/3 is enabled alongside HTTP/1 or HTTP/2. Fix the check for "All services failed" to behave again as it did before HTTP/3 was introduced: Fail if not a single socket could be setup successfully. Extend the check at the end of http_server_init to cover both the HTTP/3 and the !HTTP/3 case to detect similar issues in the future. It now returns -ENOMEM and closes all existing sockets for proper cleanup should the check fail.

problem_description: drivers: sensor: shell: fix decimal parsing of attribute values. parse_sensor_value() read the fractional part of a value with a single strtoul() and then multiplied it by 10 until it reached 100000. That discards the leading zeros, so '50.000001' and '50.1' both produced a val2 of 100000, and '50.005' produced 500000 instead of 5000. That loop also never terminates when the fraction is all zeros, since multiplying 0 by 10 never reaches 100000, so 'attr_set <dev> <chan> sampling_frequency 50.0' hung the shell thread. Parsing the fraction with base 0 was wrong as well: '50.08' was rejected as an invalid octal literal, '50.0x10' was silently accepted as hex, and strtoul() accepts a sign, so '50.-5' wrapped around to a large unsigned value. Accumulate the fraction one digit at a time and scale it to micro-units based on the number of digits that were actually given, and reject anything that is not a decimal digit. Trailing zeros beyond six digits are accepted, while a fraction that genuinely needs finer than micro-unit resolution is still rejected.

problem_description: Bluetooth: Host: Fix deadlock when data is sent during bt_disable(). bt_disable() clears BT_DEV_READY and then waits for the controller to be reset, with the connections still in place since commit 78ea662dfe39 ("Bluetooth: Host: Reset controller before conn teardown in bt_disable()"). Data sent meanwhile is dropped by send_buf(), the Host being no longer ready, which the TX processor takes for a fatal error and answers by disconnecting the connection. That is a synchronous HCI command issued from the thread that transmits commands, so it waits for a command that it cannot send, and does so holding the host lock. With CONFIG_BT_SMP bt_disable() takes that lock once the controller has been reset and never gets to purge the command queue, which would have ended the wait: both threads stay blocked until the command times out and the Host asserts. Seen with auto-pts, which powers the tester off while a broadcast source is streaming. Have the TX processor pass over the connections while the Host is not ready, before it takes anything from them. What is queued stays where it is until bt_disable() tears the connections down, as for any connection that goes away with data queued, or until the Host is ready again after a failed reset, which now restarts the TX processor. That replaces the check in send_buf(), which came too late: the upper layer had by then accounted for the data as handed over, and the failure was reported to a callback running in the TX processor. bt_disable() now clears BT_DEV_READY under the host lock, which the TX processor holds for a whole pass, so that the flag does not change under a pass that another thread is in the middle of.

problem_description: drivers: dma: mcux_edma: fix pointer casts for 64-bit hosts. The mcux_edma driver assigns pointers to and from uint32_t in several places, which truncates on 64-bit hosts (AArch64) and produces -Wpointer-to-int-cast / -Wint-to-pointer-cast warnings. On i.MX93 all DMA-visible memory happens to live below 4 GiB so the truncation is lossless today, but the pattern is unsafe on any future 64-bit NXP SoC with DRAM above 4 GiB physical. Route the conversions through uintptr_t so the compiler sees a matching-width intermediate: * Cast dma_block_config address fields through uintptr_t before handing them to EDMA_PrepareTransfer as void *. * Cast tcd (edma_tcd_t *) through uintptr_t before truncating to uint32_t for comparison against hw_id, which comes from the 32-bit EDMA_GetNextTCDAddress() hardware register. * Cast the src/dst uint32_t arguments of edma_reload_dynamic through uintptr_t before feeding them to EDMA_PrepareTransfer as void *. problem_description: samples: bluetooth: a2dp_sink: fix codec_play for runtime-MCLK boards. Three related fixes to make codec_play work on AArch64 boards whose codec MCLK is derived from a runtime-tunable clock (i.MX93 SAI3): * Round the mem_slab block size up to sizeof(void *) at 44.1 kHz. A2DP_SBC_DATA_PLAY_SIZE_44_1K (1764) is 4-byte aligned but not 8-byte aligned, so k_mem_slab_init() rejects it with -EINVAL on 64-bit targets and leaves the slab uninitialized. The backing buffer is already sized to the larger 48 kHz block, so rounding up is safe. Also propagate the k_mem_slab_init() return value to a diagnostic printk instead of silently discarding it. * Configure the I2S/SAI before the audio codec. On boards whose MCLK is derived from a runtime-tunable CCM root, i2s_configure() may retune MCLK to a sample-rate-aligned family (e.g. 11.2896 MHz for 44.1 kHz vs. 12.288 MHz for 48 kHz). If the codec is configured first it reads a stale MCLK via clock_control_get_rate() and programs its FLL for the wrong input frequency, producing an out-of-spec SYSCLK after the SAI subsequently retunes. Reordering is safe on boards with a DT-static MCLK (e.g. i.MXRT anatop PLLs). * Sleep 1 ms in the codec_keep_play() idle wait loop instead of busy-spinning at 100% CPU while audio_start is false.

problem_description: bluetooth: mesh: fix BLOB flash double-program on ECC flash. The flush runs in wr() rather than block_end so a failed flash_area_write is returned to the server (the chunk stays missing and the client retries) and a sticky error prevents any later re-program; an unaligned init offset is rejected up front. When the resolving list cannot be changed, bt_id_del() defers the removal by flagging the keys, but bt_keys_clear() wipes the keys right after, so the removal is lost. The removal has been lost this way since commit e25d925242c2 ("Bluetooth: Defer RL update if there's an ongoing connection"). Queue the peer identity address instead, so the removal survives the keys being cleared or reused. bt_id_add() carries out the queued removals before adding, so a peer added again after the deferring condition ended is not removed afterwards, and rebuilding the list after host-side resolution drops the queued removals it no longer holds. The limited scan flag is dropped as the removal is carried out right away in that case.

problem_description: drivers: dma: esp32: fix the cache maintenance around rx buffers. On a soc with a write-back data cache the controller and the cpu disagree about an rx buffer twice over. Before the transfer the cpu still owns the buffer and the controller may fill only part of it, so write the cached copy out and drop it: memory then holds the cpu data and no stale line can later be written over what the controller delivers. After the transfer the cached copy is stale and must be dropped, but the buffer rarely starts or ends on a cache line, so its two edge lines are shared with data the cpu owns and keeps writing while the transfer runs. Writing those lines back first would put a stale copy of the buffer on top of the received data, and dropping them whole would discard the cpu's writes. Save the shared bytes, invalidate whole lines, and restore them. Do this before every rx callback and not only on the end-of-frame one: a consumer reading the buffer from a block callback would otherwise see stale bytes. Round to the widest line the build uses rather than to CONFIG_DCACHE_LINE_SIZE, which holds the devicetree value and can be narrower than the line the cache is programmed with: esp32s3 picks its data cache line at startup and esp32p4 keeps a second level, and a range operation covers those whole.

problem_description: net: config: sntp: Fix race conditions in sntp resync. Fix two problems in the SNTP resync path. First, the SNTP resync could re-enable itself after the connection manager disabled it. If any async callbacks or timeouts were active when the NET_EVENT_L4_DISCONNECTED occured, they could reenqueue the sntp_resync_work after the l4_event_handler canceled it. This was a pre-existing issue in the resync code. Second, the new net_config_sntp_set_server allowed the application to schedule a resync, which did not check if there was already a resync in progress with pending async callbacks or timeouts. It would also re-enable the resync if it was disabled by the l4_event_handler. Fix both issues by tracking whether the resync is currently in progress with the sntp_resync_in_progress flag, and track if it is enabled with the sntp_resync_enabled flag. Both of these flags are protected by a mutex. The enabled flag is toggled only by the l4_event_handler. The other points where a resync can be initiated, net_config_sntp_set_server and net_config_init_clock_via_sntp, only queue the resync work if the enabled flag is set. The in_progress flag is set only by the sntp_resync_handler, and cleared on error or when the last callback in the async resync chain is reached. If the sntp_resync_handler happens to be called while the in_progress flag is already set, it reschedules itself and does nothing. This prevents multiple resyncs being active at the same time.

problem_description: pm: fix truncation of the next event tick count. pm_policy_next_event_ticks() and pm_policy_next_custom_ticks() both report int64_t tick counts, but pm_system_suspend() stored them in int32_t locals and ticks_expiring_sooner() took int32_t parameters. An event further out than INT32_MAX ticks therefore truncated, and could truncate negative: at a 32768 Hz tick rate that is only ~18.2 hours (INT32_MAX / 32768 = 65536 s) of lead time. A negative value then either trips the __ASSERT() guards in ticks_expiring_sooner() or, in a build without assertions, wins the MIN() and discards the real kernel deadline. In the latter case pm_policy_next_state() receives a negative tick count, which the default policy compares against an unsigned min_residency_ticks, so the loop never breaks and the deepest state is selected while a much nearer wakeup is still pending. Widen ticks_expiring_sooner() to int64_t and clamp its result to the [-1, SYS_CLOCK_MAX_WAIT] range that pm_policy_next_state() accepts, so the policy hook keeps its int32_t tick parameter while a far future event can no longer wrap negative and be read as "nothing pending". kernel/idle.c already relies on the same upper bound when it narrows z_get_next_timeout_expiry() into _kernel.idle. Detect "nothing pending" by testing the sign rather than by comparing against K_TICKS_FOREVER. K_TICKS_FOREVER is ((k_ticks_t)-1) and k_ticks_t is uint32_t when CONFIG_TIMEOUT_64BIT=n, so at int64_t width that sentinel promotes to 4294967295 and never compares equal to the -1 the callers actually pass. The same asymmetry is already documented on SYS_CLOCK_IDLE_FOREVER. The mismatch dates back to commit 59779ebe4b12 ("pm: policy: event: use uptime ticks"), which widened pm_policy_next_event_ticks() to int64_t without updating its caller.

problem_description: net: lib: dns: Fix post-CNAME query cancellation. Fix a bug where a device failing DNS resolution get a runtime fault. The issue is that dns_resolve_cancel_with_name() finds a query by `query_hash` for cancellation. But internally, the resolve module updates query_hash as the resolution follows CNAME aliases. As a result, after one CNAME hop or more, the caller becomes unable to cancel its own query. The failure to cancel a DNS query results is serious and leads to a **use-after-return bug**. This is because zsock_getaddrinfo() does this: 1. Calls resolve module with a callback user data set to runtime stack variable ai_state. 2. On timeout, tries to cancels the query then returns. If cancellation failed, the query is still present in the resolve module and when it eventually times out, will run the user callback with data pointed at a now stale stack frame. This fix keeps track of the original query hash in addition to the current one, allowing the caller to cancel reliably.

problem_description: tests: subsys: fs: fat_fs_api: fix stale cache on partition wipe. wipe_partition is called as part of the mkfs test such that the filesystem header can be in an invalid state and a mount will fail before attempting to format the storage device with a valid filesystem. It presently calls flash_area_flatten, which successfully wipes the header but bypasses the caching logic of the Disk Access API. This can result in the following mount actually succeeding from the cached header and the test failing (as the mount is asserted to fail). flash_area_flatten is implemented for devices without explicit erase functionality, while disk_access_erase is not, so we can't just bump a level higher straightforwardly. However, we can use a standard Disk Access API write to write zeroes into our buffer, which successfully updates the cache. This is actually already implemented for non-flash devices but gated behind an ifdef, so let's just make this unconditional.

problem_description: drivers: wifi: nrf_wifi: Fix raw TX with controlled-port dormant logic. A station went operational on carrier ON, which is at association, so the IP stack transmitted during the 4-way handshake and the TX path had to drop those frames. Wait for the controlled port instead; EAPOL is unaffected as it flows out-of-band through nrf_wifi_wpa_tx_control_port(). Injection has neither an association nor a controlled port, so keep the interface operational for it, gated on the carrier to match the CARR_STATE_ON check in nrf_wifi_if_send(). Read txinjection_mode from the FMAC VIF context, since a driver-side copy would go stale across down/up and MODE_SET_DONE. Move the decision into nrf_wifi_iface_operational() and let callers just request a re-evaluation. Start and stop clear the per-session state, because net_if_up() and net_if_down() leave the dormant flag as they found it. Take vif_lock for the oper-state decision. The handler reads txinjection_mode through rpu_ctx, and nrf_wifi_fmac_dev_rem_zep() frees that context before clearing the pointer, so a handler in flight could dereference freed memory. nrf_wifi_if_stop_zep() frees under vif_lock, so holding it for the read serialises the two.

problem_description: drivers: pwm: fix capture fall-through when timeout is K_NO_WAIT. Passing a wait of K_NO_WAIT to the pwm_capture_cycles() function causes the k_sem_take function to return -EBUSY unless the capture has completed. This condition is not tested for and causes the function to ignore the error case and allow the function to use capture status and data values that have not been initialized, reporting success whenever the data happens to be zero. The capture is also left armed with a pointer to the stack frame being unwound. A single capture cannot complete without waiting, so change the pwm_capture_cycles() function to reject a K_NO_WAIT timeout with -EINVAL before configuring a capture. Update the API documentation to reflect this behavior.

problem_description: usb: host: fix control transfer ownership in usbh_req_setup. usbh_req_setup() waits on a single global semaphore with no mutual exclusion, so two threads can be inside it at once: enumeration runs on the bus thread while the shell and class drivers call in from their own. The first completion wakes an arbitrary waiter, which then reads xfer->err on a transfer that has not finished. Serialize the request with a mutex so the semaphore has one owner at a time. Timing out also released the transfer while the controller still owned it. uhc_ep_dequeue() only requests cancellation: the transfer stays with the driver until it is returned through the completion callback, and the driver may still write into its buffer. Callers such as usbh_req_desc_dev() free that buffer as soon as usbh_req_setup() returns, so a cancelled transfer could land in a recycled net_buf. Wait for the completion callback before freeing, and drop the callback's -ECONNRESET path now that the caller always owns the transfer.

problem_description: bluetooth: audio: fix null pointer deref in media proxy. Currently, synchronous controller functions in media_proxy.c blindly dereference local player callbacks. This triggers a hard fault if a local player has not been registered or if it does not implement all optional callbacks (leaving some function pointers as NULL). This commit adds validation guards to verify that mprx.local_player.calls and the individual callback function pointers are not NULL across all synchronous media control getters and setters. If a callback is unimplemented, a safe fallback value (e.g., "" for strings, 0U for integers) is returned instead. Additionally, it relaxes the check in media_proxy_pl_register to allow partial implementation of callbacks during player registration, as allowed by the public contract in media_proxy.h, while still preventing a completely NULL callback table from being registered.

problem_description: Revert "kernel: Fixed init_delay initialization on older GCC versions". This reverts commit 52a1db1cf331df0e72f2024b475de053f862e688. Splitting Z_TIMEOUT_TICKS_INIT, Z_TIMEOUT_NO_WAIT_INIT, and SYS_TIMEOUT_MS_INIT was introduced to avoid using compound literals in static initializers, which caused "initializer element is not constant" errors on GCC versions prior to 5.1. problem_description: drivers: wifi: native_sim: Fix nl80211 connect command race. Connecting sometimes hung with an endless flood of "nl80211: send_and_recv->nl_recvmsgs failed: -4 (Try again)". -4 is libnl NLE_AGAIN: the non-blocking netlink socket has no data and hostap's send_and_recv() busy-loops until the command's ACK arrives. The host adapter runs two threads: the eloop thread (host_handler) services the nl80211 event sockets, including bss->nl_connect, while the Zephyr supplicant thread issued the authenticate/associate/deauthenticate ops with send_and_recv() on that same bss->nl_connect socket. When a connect command ran on the Zephyr thread while the eloop thread was also reading bss->nl_connect, the eloop could consume the command's ACK, leaving send_and_recv() spinning on NLE_AGAIN forever. It was intermittent because it is a race over which thread reads the socket first. Run those three MLME commands on the thread that owns the netlink sockets instead. A small command-handoff (cmd_fd/cmd_done_fd socketpair plus pending_cmd) lets the Zephyr caller publish a request, wake the eloop, and block until the eloop thread has executed the op; the argument is passed by pointer since both threads share one address space. With a single thread doing the netlink I/O there is no concurrent reader to steal the ACK. Only the bss->nl_connect commands are marshalled. Scan and the other ops use global->nl, which the eloop does not service, so they are not raced and stay on the Zephyr thread; moving the scan path onto the eloop thread was observed to starve event processing and perturb scan timing. Tested on native_sim against the net-tools mac80211_hwsim setup: the interop test passes 5/5 across repeated runs and rapid connect/disconnect cycles no longer produce the "Try again" flood.
commit_subject: drivers: wifi: native_sim: Add Wi-Fi driver using host nl80211
fix_subject: drivers: wifi: native_sim: Fix nl80211 connect command race
